summary: Isaiah includes thornbushes among the places where the fly and the bee will settle. Later he pictures the cypress growing where the thornbush once stood.

senses.definition: A prickly bush growing in the open country.

evidence.note: The insects called from Egypt and Assyria settle among the thornbushes as well as in ravines and rock clefts.
The cypress replaces the thornbush, just as the myrtle replaces the sirpād.

evidence.locator: entry 9218, nʿāṣā, including the prick of a plant

note: The repeated final ṣ may form a plant name from a verb meaning ‘stick in’ or ‘prick’. The Aramaic verbs support that possibility, though neither identifies a particular shrub.
